- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >75), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to avoid overreaction.  
- If recent sentiment is mixed or mildly positive (e.g., -0.1 to 0.1), model often underestimates upward momentum; increase forecast mid-range by 2–5% to capture mean reversion bias.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon; add 1–3% buffer to initial forecast values, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- When sentiment shows recent reversal (e.g., from negative to neutral), model lags in recognizing trend shift; adjust forecast to align with sentiment reversal 1–2 days ahead.
